findings.where: Hero, the standfirst under the heading: "Over 40 years of international infrastructure experience"
findings.fault: The last line of the standfirst claims seniority with a count of years, which nobody can check. Next to it sits a checkable fact, "former Lead Lawyer in the World Bank's PPP Group", and the count of years weakens that fact by putting it beside a boast.
findings.who_objects: A procurement officer at a development bank reads experience by project, body and region, as their selection rules ask. To them "40 years" is an adjective, the big-firm boast the brief's client value 6 rules out, and it says nothing about whether Mark has done work like theirs.

findings.where: Hero, the standfirst and heading together (the 5-second test)
findings.fault: The first screen says what Mark does (advice on infrastructure projects and the laws behind them) but not who it is for or where. It never names development banks, agencies or governments as the clients, or the regions of his work. "International" is the only clue to place.
findings.who_objects: A first-time visitor from a multilateral bank, who must decide in seconds whether this advisor works for bodies like theirs in their region. That is the first thing first-visit trust says an advisor's visitor must be sure of (items 2 and 6). Here they have to guess.

findings.where: Hero, the "Get in touch" button (mailto:Mark.Moseley@MMMinfra.com); the nav's "Contact" link goes nowhere (#)
findings.fault: The only contact route is a button that opens a mail program. The email address is never shown as text a visitor can read or copy.
findings.who_objects: A bank staff member on a locked-down work machine or using webmail, where mailto does nothing or opens the wrong program. They are left with no address, at the one moment the page asks them to act. First-visit trust item 7 asks for the address in full as its own link text.

findings.where: Article specimen, the lecture row: "Streamlining the PPP Process: Meeting the 'Abundance' Challenge — Lecture · 23 April 2026 · PDF"
findings.fault: The lecture is listed with a date and a format but no venue or host. That leaves out the part that shows standing: who asked Mark to speak.
findings.who_objects: A reader who hires through procurement takes standing from who asked for the work. A talk with no named venue reads as unverifiable. Feel the CV asks for the newest talk with its venue.

findings.where: Hero, next to the "Get in touch" button
findings.fault: Next to the call to action there is no outside proof: no link out to a report, law or project page that a named body hosts and that shows Mark's work. The only evidence is his own statement of his former role.
findings.who_objects: A careful development-agency officer checking an unknown consultant before writing. They would want one link they can follow to a source they trust. No testimonials or logos are held, so item 14's fallback (links out to work that named bodies host) is the honest form, and it is missing.
